title: Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay - Lets Play and Review - Part 6
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dFH36q7iWiU

Tank is face-down on the cobbles. Daniel (@dungeondive) opens this **Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay** session laying out the three ways to rally a downed hero — spend your own action, spend an ally's, or burn a health potion — and notes the quiet cost: every knockdown drops the morale track, and morale at zero ends the campaign run outright.

Ross fails three rally attempts in a row. Tank eventually hauls himself up on his own third try, heals half, and the session settles into a grinding clear-out of grunts while Daniel wrestles a rules ambiguity aloud: stepping up the initiative track appears to let a hero take two turns back to back. He can't convince himself that's intended, rules against his own heroes, and says he'll correct it later if he's wrong.

The turn comes from the event deck. Trixie offers two treasures outright, with a knowledge-check puzzle for a third at the risk of morale — he takes the free pair and declines the gamble. Out come a Tidal Blast and a convention-exclusive Dragon Bow, comfortably the best weapon he's seen in the game. Tank's ability to wield two-handed weapons one-handed means he keeps his shield; Ross gives his up. He also admits, cheerfully, to knocking both XP trackers off the table.

----

Offered two guaranteed treasures or a puzzle for a third, Daniel took the sure thing. When do you gamble against a morale track?
